newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: LatAm stocks seen aiming for new lofty levels.
newsitem.headline: LatAm stocks seen aiming for new lofty levels.

text.p: Stocks were seen pushing higher in Latin America's bullish stock markets this week after key mid-term elections in Mexico Sunday passed quietly, dealers said.

Analysts welcomed the absence of fraud allegations that marred previous elections, saying the graceful defeat of the ruling party was more important than the results, which had already been discounted.

Early tallies showed President Ernesto Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) lost overall control of the lower house for the first time since 1929, as well Mexico City, the country's nerve center.
Analysts said the bolsa still had upside potential thanks to heavy foreign investment flows, although profit-taking would be healthy after a recent sharp rally.
"Consolidation would be good for the market, but heavy foreign capital inflow means we cannot be sure share prices will hold back," said Gerardo Copca at Finamex brokerage.
The Mexican bolsa's blue-chip IPC index .MXX gained 3.7 percent last week to close at a record 4,644.60 points.
In Brazil stocks, were likely to keep climbing on fresh purchases by local equity funds. "It's money from domestic funds that is lifting the market," one senior trader said.
The rise could be moderate, however, after a 90 percent surge in share prices so far this year.
Analysts also awaited developments in the closely-watched "Band B" cellular selloff.

The Communications Ministry is due to open the bids for the Sao Paulo region Wednesday and traders expect them to be considerably higher than the minimum price asked by the government. Last week, the Bovespa index .BVSP of the 47 most traded shares rose 5.7 percent to 13,493 points.
Argentine stocks were also seen headed higher, driven by strength on the U.S. markets and talk of a foreign debt buyback plan, dealers said.
The bolsa's blue-chip MerVal index .MERV jumped 3.5 percent last week to close at a new five-year high of 837.95.
"The MerVal will aim for 850-860 in the near term, provided U.S. rates stay low," said Gabriel Ruiz at brokers Tavelli. He recommended stocks in the construction, steel and agriculture sectors.
"The bolsa is still looking good and if the government finally announces a buyback program it would give it an extra boost," another dealer said.
Brokers expected Chilean shares to push modestly higher on confidence that imminent second quarter earnings reports will be strong, with profit-taking tempering gains, brokers said.

But a two-month-old bull run has made the bourse expensive, and some brokers saw a cooling-off period ahead. "Sometime in the next few weeks this market is going to have to take a rest. The IPSA is already above most people's forecasts for the whole year," one trader said.

Shares in the telecommunications sector, for example, may pause after a rally in the last few weeks on the imminent merger between Compaa de Telecomunicaciones and competitor VTR. Telephone stocks may also take a breather.
The blue-chip IPSA index ended Friday at 137.24 points, up 4.2 percent for the whole week.
Continuing interest in Venezuelan market bellwether Electricidad de Caracas, which recently hiked tariffs 75 percent, was seen keeping the increasingly expensive Caracas market strong, dealers said.

"As long as there is demand for Electricidad, the rest of the market is unlikely to fall," said Eduardo Soto, president of Delta brokerage. The utility company accounts for up to one third of market volume.
Caracas stocks surged over 35 percent in June on foreign bidding.
The rise was barely checked by a brief spate of profit-taking last week when the 19-share .IBC index closed up 7.5 percent at 9,467.44 points.
((-- Buenos Aires Newsroom 541 318-0657))
